summary: RedCap is a mature local skill-root runtime with a CLI facade, package safety gate and clean workspace E2E. P4-2k narrowed the npm candidate surface to a curated runtime-readiness profile; RASG-020 now adds an explicit public-runtime versus maintainer-tool contract boundary. The remaining public-release blockers are explicit human release decisions plus R1 boundary blockers for internal-control-plane, prism-layer-and-evidence and internal-layer-a.

observed_facts.source_visibility_model: npm package source must be treated as visible to users

findings.claim: The current package surface passes the publish safety gate, including content scanning for local user home paths, and excludes known local secrets, runtime residue and private knowledge paths.
The package identity is now prepared as the user-approved @norven63/redcap across package.json and runtime package readiness policy while keeping private=true and publish_allowed=false.
The package is deliberately still private and publish_allowed=false. That is correct for P4-2d readiness work, but a separate release task must explicitly enable publication before npm publish.

P4-2k keeps the existing compatibility wrappers and adds a package-visible runtime import map that separates the public runtime contract from repo-maintenance tooling. Full physical movement of compass/tools and prism/tools remains a later maintainer refactor, but it is no longer a release-path ambiguity. CLI diagnose now defaults to the runtime profile while the source repo keeps the full maintenance profile.

P4-2c adds publish-grade doctor, debug --json, --trace, help and structured error surfaces. The checker verifies external workspace and self-development smoke tests, redacted debug output, no raw internal diagnose dump, and cause/impact/suggested_action errors.

P4-2b makes workspace-oriented CLI commands resolve a managed project workspace by default. status, diagnose and change-intake now support --workspace/--task-file, default task state to <workspace>/.dev-task.md, and expose runtime root, workspace root, task file and user-state policy in status/diagnose output.
package.json currently declares UNLICENSED. That is acceptable while private=true, but a public npm release needs an explicit distribution/license decision before publish.

The R1 internal-control-plane blocker remains unresolved. P4-2p made the split contract auditable and P4-2s adds a dry-run target map, but neither physically splits compass/references nor claims release-safe completion.
The R1 prism-layer-and-evidence blocker remains unresolved. P4-2q made Prism tools, reports and run evidence boundaries auditable, but did not physically split or clean Prism evidence.

The R1 internal-layer-a blocker remains unresolved. P4-2r proves loom is absent from package candidates and records its consumers, but does not decide whether Layer A is public product, retired, moved or excluded.

P4-2m, P4-2n, P4-2o and P4-2p keep the package candidate surface inside the curated alpha-readiness cap while adding historical asset cleanup, Evolution harvest, R1 disposition preflight and control-plane contract split preflight gates as explicit metadata. The present count is 202. The alpha readiness surface remains curated, while the formal public release task must decide whether to trim repo-governance checks into a smaller runtime profile or split a maintainer profile.

redcap-arsenal now contains a first RedCap Forge-reviewed append-only public entry set, metadata index and Norven namespace, but this does not make redcap-arsenal mature, complete, or safe to market as a populated shared knowledge/skill arsenal.
The release posture now treats npm package contents as visible source and relies on exclusion of secrets rather than obfuscation.

P4-2k adds a public release handoff, and RASG-020 further separates ordinary runtime commands from maintainer release-readiness commands: normal users start with revive/status/doctor/diagnose/debug/closeout, while package-manifest/publish-safety/package-surface/pre-release-review remain maintainer preparation tools. Formal publish actions remain a separate authorized release task.

must_not_claim: Do not claim RedCap is public-release-ready.
Do not claim P4-2 public release is complete.
Do not claim redcap-arsenal is mature or complete because it contains a first reviewed-substantive entry set.
Do not claim npm source is hidden from users.
Do not claim P4-2i's minimum runtime layout equals a full execution-layer split.
Do not claim clean workspace E2E equals a multi-OS external release matrix.
